messages:
oliver: quick ping :eyes: — can someone take a look at PR #2847? It's a small change to the batcher defaults + a new quant mode. I ran local smoke but want a second pair of eyes before merging.

maria: link? happy to glance in a bit.

oliver: https://git.redwood.com/redwood/inference/pull/2847 — main changes in runtime/config/batcher.yaml and runtime/quant/driver.cc

aj: I'll run the perf suite on dedicated and post numbers. what's the expected cost delta?

oliver: rough estimates from my bench: p95 latency +6%, throughput steady, token cost ~ -22% (due to lower quant bits + smaller batches). Worth noting: this increases CPU pre/post processing a bit.

jess: can you paste the config snippet you're changing? makes it faster to reason about.

oliver: sure, snippet below:

```yaml
batcher:
  max_batch_size: 64  # -> 48
  max_latency_ms: 20  # shrank to 12 in pilot
  enable_priority_routing: true

quant:
  mode: dynamic
  bits: 4  # 8 -> 4 for the main weights, small layers left at 8
  fallback_to_fp16: true
```

rkumar: quick thought — with smaller batch sizes we might hit more scheduling overhead on the 8-GPU p4d nodes. Did you try the new kernel selection flag? (runtime/exec/select_kernels=true)

oliver: yes, enabled. I added a heuristic to prefer grouped matmuls when batch < 32. See the comment in driver.cc.

dev-bot: CI: build passed · unit tests passed · perf-suite: failed (regression detected) · details: https://ci.redwood.com/builds/39021

aj: thanks — I'll pick up CI, run full perf with canary routing (50/50) and dedicated pool. ETA ~30m.

jess: left one inline comment about cache eviction timing — if we shrink batches we should avoid aggressive KV cache trimming during spikes. small nit.

oliver: good catch, I added a tweak: kv_cache.eviction_threshold_ms += 20 on pilot.

maria: I can review code now. offer: if perf numbers look good I'm +1 on merging and doing a staged canary.

aj: perf run done. p50 latency +3%, p95 +7% on small seq (512) workloads. cost estimate for typical chat workload: -24%. No correctness regressions in generation tests.

jess: sounds reasonable. would prefer we hold canary at 10% for 2 hours first.

oliver: yeah let's do 10% for 2h then 50% for 1h then full. I'll add rollout policy in the PR description.

maria: approved.

rkumar: approved with one comment resolved.

oliver: thanks all — merging now. will post the rollout plan and metrics channel once canary starts. :shipit:

dev-bot: Deploy triggered: canary (10%) · commit: 9a3f7b2 · monitor: infra/telemetry

jess: watching metrics, ping me if p95 > baseline +10%

oliver: noted, will update.
